content.value_statement: Go teams need help with concurrency, performance, and production architecture. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through modern Go design, testing, and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Designs Go services, CLIs, and microservices using idiomatic project structure.
Explains concurrency patterns such as worker pools, pipelines, cancellation, and graceful shutdown.
Recommends profiling, benchmarking, memory tuning, and pprof workflows for performance work.
Guides API work across net/http, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSockets, middleware, authentication, and rate limiting.
Plans database access, pooling, transactions, migrations, and query optimization for Go applications.
Suggests testing, CI/CD, Docker, Kubernetes, observability, and static analysis practices.
limitations: Does not execute Go code, run benchmarks, or inspect repositories unless the host agent provides tool access.
Depends on project context, Go version, and runtime constraints supplied by the user.
Cannot guarantee production readiness without tests, metrics, security review, and deployment validation.
May need updates for future Go releases and library changes.

use_cases.title: Design Concurrent Services
use_cases.description: Plan goroutine lifecycles, cancellation, backpressure, and error handling for a service under load.

use_cases.title: Review Go Architecture
use_cases.description: Assess interfaces, package boundaries, dependency flow, and deployment patterns before a major release.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Add health checks, logging, metrics, container builds, and CI practices for Go applications.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Go Project Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Go service for [domain]. Include packages, data flow, testing plan, and required tools.

prompt_templates.title: Review Concurrency Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this concurrency design for [task]. Check goroutine ownership, channels, cancellation, shutdown, and race risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Checking a concurrent feature before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Go performance issue: [symptoms]. Suggest profiling steps, benchmark strategy, likely bottlenecks, and safe optimization changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reducing latency, memory use, or CPU cost.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production Go microservice architecture for [requirements]. Cover APIs, persistence, observability, deployment, failure handling, and security controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning a production service with operational requirements.

output_examples.input: A team needs a high-throughput worker pool for image jobs.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering queue ownership, bounded workers, context cancellation, retry policy, metrics, benchmarks, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A Go API has growing latency and memory use.
output_examples.output: A profiling workflow using pprof, focused benchmarks, allocation review, connection pool checks, and measurable acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: A service needs production deployment guidance.
output_examples.output: A deployment checklist covering health endpoints, structured logs, Prometheus metrics, Docker builds, Kubernetes resources, CI checks, and rollback steps.

best_practices: Provide Go version, workload shape, latency targets, and deployment environment before asking for architecture advice.
Share relevant package boundaries, concurrency flows, and failure modes when requesting a review.
Ask for tests, benchmarks, and observability changes alongside implementation guidance.
anti_patterns: Requesting broad rewrites without giving current constraints, interfaces, or operational goals.
Optimizing code before measuring with benchmarks, traces, or production metrics.
Ignoring cancellation, timeouts, and error propagation in concurrent Go designs.

faq.question: Does this skill write Go code?
faq.answer: It can guide code design and implementation when the agent has repository context and edit tools.

faq.question: Which Go versions does it target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Go 1.21 and newer patterns, including generics, workspaces, slog, profiling, and modern tooling.

faq.question: Can it help with performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests profiling, benchmarks, allocation review, pprof, tracing, and measurable optimization steps.

faq.question: Can it review concurrency risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks goroutine ownership, channel use, cancellation, locking, race risks, and graceful shutdown.

faq.question: Does it deploy services automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend Docker, Kubernetes, CI, metrics, and rollout practices, but deployment requires user-approved tooling.

faq.question: Is it only for web services?
faq.answer: No. It also supports CLIs, libraries, background workers, data pipelines, and platform tooling written in Go.
